rv.q: The end result is a richly resonant comedy that reminds us that, while Simon may be pure, he is rarely simple.
Watching DeVito on stage is a privilege, without a doubt, but this isn't comedy at his most deliciously fresh.
Thea Sharrock's limp revival of the 1972. Neil Simon play The Sunshine Boys tries to get equivalent comic mileage out of the difference in size between DeVito and our own Richard Griffiths.
The play resonates with wonderful cross-talk and gag-spinning, from the minute DeVito hears his kitchen kettle whistling and picks up the telephone receiver with a bemused “Hello.”

cn.t: DeVito shines in his West End debut, bringing energy and expert timing to this Neil Simon revival, though the production itself receives mixed reviews. Critics praise the leads' chemistry but question the staging's overall vitality.
